safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase safety lead time from 0.0 to 4.85 days

narrative: Material PL3__M27982FE shows strongly lumpy demand with a significant upward trend of approximately 2.61 units/day over the observation period (Mar 2025 – Mar 2026). Demand CV of 1.56 combined with 23% zero-demand days classifies this as lumpy. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.39), oscillating between 1.46 and 4.99 days. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy was selected to respond promptly to demand spikes; a safety stock of 840 units (z=1.645 × sigma_LTD=511) protects the 95% service level while an EOQ of 5,087 units reduces replenishment events from ~65 to ~9 per year, cutting total costs by ~69%.
warnings: Strong upward demand trend detected (+2.61 units/day): recalibrate safety stock and EOQ quarterly.
Lead time instability (CV=0.386): monitor supplier reliability; consider dual-sourcing.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy, trending demand with unstable lead times requires a continuous-review trigger to catch demand spikes early. The (r,Q) model fires a fixed replenishment order Q=5087 whenever inventory drops to the reorder point r=1360, combining EOQ economics with safety-stock protection at the 95th-percentile service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Demand variability dominates buffer variance at 84.6%. With an accelerating demand trend, the current safety stock of 840 units may become insufficient within 2-3 quarters if the trend persists. Annual recalibration is recommended as a minimum.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (696) + safety stock (840) = 1,536 units, well below max storage (31,181). No capacity or MOQ infeasibility conflict.
